description.value: The study examined how schizophrenia diagnosis and chronic cannabis use interact to influence behavioural and neural sensitivity during reward anticipation.

design.value: A 2 × 2 factorial, between-group study compared cannabis-user and non-cannabis-user healthy controls with cannabis-user and non-cannabis-user schizophrenia patients during a two-choice reward anticipation reaction-time task with functional MRI. Behavioural analyses used ANCOVA models with reward condition as a within-subject factor and age and education as covariates; imaging analyses used ROI-based second-level ANCOVA models.

task_name.value: two-choice RT task with elements of the MID and Eriksen flanker tasks

task_description.value: Participants responded to a series of five arrow heads with their right or left index finger according to the pointing direction of the central arrowhead, preceded by valence and magnitude cues and followed by feedback.

instructions.value: The participant was informed that the aim of the task was to gain a maximal amount of points and in order for them to win (+) or avoid losing (–), they must respond both accurately and quickly.

stimuli.value: Only the incongruent configuration of the arrow heads was used (< < > < < or > > < > >). Valence cues were + (win), − (lose) or * (neutral), and magnitude cues represented high: 20, low: 5, or none: 0.

description.value: Functional MR images were acquired using echo-planar imaging with 36 slices and 3 × 3 × 3 mm voxel size.

Images were realigned, temporally interpolated, segmented using the T1 image, normalized to standard MNI space and smoothed.

steps.value: Temporal interpolation to correct for delay in slice acquisition

Smoothing with an 8 mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel
Applying a high-pass filter of 128 s cut off

model_settings.value: A 2 × 2 × 5 ANCOVA design with reward condition as the within-subject repeated measures factor, cannabis use and schizophrenia as between-group fixed factors, and education level and age as continuous covariates; contrast analyses used a GLM 2 × 2 ANCOVA.

Three regressors, reward (+), punishment (−) and neutral (*), were included for the valence model. Five regressors (−20, −5, 0, +5, +20) were included for the magnitude model. Motion correction parameters estimated from realignment were additional regressors. T-contrasts measured valence, reward versus punishment and magnitude.
A 2 × 2 ANCOVA assessed modulation of each contrast with cannabis use, schizophrenia status and their interaction, with years of education and age as covariates.
One-sample t-tests were carried out for each contrast within predefined reward-related ROIs.
